literature.headline_zh: SARS-CoV-2本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期SARS-CoV-2研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 青少年对 Omicron BA.1、WH1、Beta 和 Delta 变异株的中和抗体滴度以及总结合抗体水平显著高于年轻成人(P < .001)。跨变异株的抗体滴度在第 336 天仍高于基线(第 0 天)。不良事件主要为轻度/中度,28 天内最常见的不良事件是注射部位疼痛和头痛。未报告严重不良事件。 [10.1542/peds.2026-076225]
严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 暴露诱导了 MERS-CoV 抗体,主要针对保守的 S2 结构域,偶尔具有中和能力。 [10.3201/eid3211.260690]
综述揭示了不同研究中Mpro动力学参数存在较大差异,这影响了研究之间的比较以及抑制剂功效的评估。 [10.1007/s11033-026-12966-6]
通过虚拟筛选,确定索拉非尼(sorafenib)为一种有前景的变构抑制剂。分子动力学模拟显示,索拉非尼结合会导致NSP1的构象和动态变化,从而实现蛋白质稳定化。 [10.1007/s00894-026-07031-9]
对于广泛定义的有症状感染,汇总的相对VE(rVE)为51%(95% CI:39%,60%),对于需要医疗干预的有症状感染,汇总的rVE为19%(95% CI:12%,25%),表明疫苗接种显著降低了从有症状感染进展到住院的风险。严重程度的减轻效果随时间保持稳定,且不因疫苗平台而显著不同,但在≥60岁的老年人中减轻程度较低。 [10.1093/cid/ciag346]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。

From 2021 to 2022, the proportion of vulvar ulcers among reported adverse events exceeded the upper control limits for the first time since 2002. Most cases (134/137, 97.8%) were linked to COVID-19 vaccines. Ad26.COV2.S had the highest relative risk (2.72 vs. BNT162b2; 95% CI: 1.17-6.30). [10.1016/j.tjog.2026.06.009]
The review revealed large variability in kinetic parameters across studies, which compromises comparisons and the evaluation of inhibitor efficacy. [10.1007/s11033-026-12966-6]

Sorafenib was identified as a promising allosteric inhibitor through virtual screening. Molecular dynamics simulations showed that sorafenib binding leads to conformational and dynamic changes in NSP1, resulting in protein stabilization. [10.1007/s00894-026-07031-9]

papers.title: SARS-CoV-2 Vaccination and Attenuation of Breakthrough Infection Severity: A Systematic Global Review and Meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccines provide strong protection against severe outcomes but do not fully prevent infection, and the extent to which they attenuate disease severity among breakthrough infections remains unclear. Existing evidence is limited by small sample sizes, potential selection bias, and inconsistent findings. METHODS: We conducted a systematic selection and meta-analysis of studies identified from a living systematic review of global observational studies reporting vaccine effectiveness (VE) against symptomatic infection and hospitalization. We computed the relative VE (rVE) against hospitalization versus symptomatic infection for matched VE pairs, representing vaccine-induced attenuation of severity. Multilevel meta-analysis and metaregression were used to pool estimates and assess effect modifiers. RESULTS: A total of 184 VE pairs from 37 studies were included. The pooled rVE was 51% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 39%, 60%) for broadly defined symptomatic infection and 19% (95% CI: 12%, 25%) for medically attended symptomatic infection, indicating significant attenuation of disease severity among vaccinated cases. Given substantial heterogeneity, interpretation focused on stratified and adjusted analyses. Attenuation was lower in older adults aged ≥60 years and showed no significant waning over time. Variant patterns differed by endpoint definition: attenuation was weaker for Omicron subvariants when broadly defined symptomatic infection was the comparator. No significant differences were observed between vaccine platforms. CONCLUSIONS: COVID-19 vaccination markedly reduces the risk of progression from symptomatic infection to hospitalization. Attenuation of severity was sustained over time and did not differ significantly by vaccine platform but was lower in older adults and varied by symptomatic-infection definition and variant period.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic global review and meta-analysis evaluates the effectiveness of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines in reducing the severity of breakthrough infections. The study includes 184 vaccine effectiveness (VE) pairs from 37 observational studies, analyzing the relative VE against hospitalization and medically attended symptomatic infection. The pooled rVE was 51% and 19%, respectively, indicating significant attenuation of disease severity among vaccinated individuals. However, the evidence is limited by small sample sizes, selection bias, and heterogeneity, with lower attenuation observed in older adults and for Omicron subvariants. The findings suggest that vaccination markedly reduces the risk of progression to hospitalization, with no significant differences by vaccine platform. Research should focus on understanding variability in attenuation across different definitions and variant periods, and surveillance should account for these factors to optimize public health strategies.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述探讨了严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗 在降低突破性感染严重程度方面的有效性,重点关注住院和有症状感染结果。核心问题是:疫苗接种 是否能减轻那些尽管接种疫苗仍感染的人的疾病严重程度。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一项系统性的全球分析和观察性研究的元分析。它包括37项研究,共184对疫苗效力(VE)数据,采用多层次元分析和元回归方法来汇总估计值并评估效应修饰因素。该方法涉及计算针对住院与有症状感染的相对疫苗效力(rVE)以匹配的疫苗效力对进行分析。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 对于广泛定义的有症状感染,汇总的相对VE(rVE)为51%(95% CI:39%,60%),对于需要医疗干预的有症状感染,汇总的rVE为19%(95% CI:12%,25%),表明疫苗接种显著降低了从有症状感染进展到住院的风险。严重程度的减轻效果随时间保持稳定,且不因疫苗平台而显著不同,但在≥60岁的老年人中减轻程度较低。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 证据受到样本量小、潜在选择偏倚和不一致结果的限制。注意到存在显著异质性,因此分析重点放在分层和调整后的分析上。此外,根据有症状感染的定义和变异时期的不同,减轻效果存在差异,当以广泛定义的有症状感染作为比较时,对奥密克戎亚变种的减轻效果较弱。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 需要进一步研究以解决不同有症状感染定义和变异时期之间减轻效果的差异。监测和诊断策略应考虑这些因素,同时应监测疫苗在老年人中的有效性,以确保其对严重结果的持续保护。

papers.title: Immunogenicity and Safety of Coadministration of AS01E-Adjuvanted Respiratory Syncytial Virus Prefusion F Protein Vaccine and a COVID-19 mRNA Vaccine in Adult s Aged ≥50 Years: A Phase 3, Randomized, Noninferiority Trial.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: This trial evaluated coadministration of the AS01E-adjuvanted respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prefusion F protein-based vaccine (adjuvanted RSVPreF3) and an Omicron XBB.1.5-based coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) mRNA vaccine in ≥50-year-olds. METHODS: This phase 3, open-label, multicenter trial randomized ≥50-year-olds 1:1 to coadministration (Co-Ad group) or sequential administration approximately 1 month apart (Control group) of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 and the COVID-19 mRNA vaccine. Primary objectives were to demonstrate noninferiority of humoral immune responses at 1 month postvaccination in terms of RSV-A, RSV-B, and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) neutralizing titers, with the upper limit of the 95% CI of adjusted geometric mean titer (GMT) group ratios (Control/Co-Ad) ≤1.50. Secondary objectives included assessment of reactogenicity up to 4 days and safety up to 6 months after vaccination. Noninferiority was achieved for RSV-A (GMT ratio: 1.12 [95% CI: .97-1.28]) and RSV-B (GMT ratio: 1.08 [95% CI: .94-1.23]) and marginally missed for SARS-CoV-2 Omicron XBB.1.5 (GMT ratio: 1.31 [95% CI: 1.13-1.51]). Within 4 days postvaccination, the most frequently reported solicited events were administration-site pain, myalgia, and fatigue. Most solicited events were of mild-to-moderate intensity, and the overall median duration was ≤3 days and comparable between groups. Unsolicited and serious adverse events were generally balanced between groups. CONCLUSIONS: Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 coadministered with a COVID-19 mRNA vaccine maintained an acceptable safety profile in ≥50-year-olds. The marginal miss of the noninferiority criterion for SARS-CoV-2 does not suggest clinically relevant interference. Therefore, the results support the coadministration of these vaccines. CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials.gov.
papers.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America

The study's results do not indicate clinically relevant interference between the vaccines, and the evidence is strong given the design and outcomes.

papers.title: Immunogenicity and Safety of PHH-1V COVID-19 Vaccine as a Heterologous Booster in Adolescents.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: PHH-1V, a protein-based, non-mRNA, bivalent, adjuvanted COVID-19 vaccine, has demonstrated strong immunogenicity and favorable safety as a booster in adults. This study evaluated PHH-1V as a heterologous booster in adolescents. METHODS: HIPRA-HH-3 was a phase IIb, open-label, multicenter, noninferiority trial assessing the immunogenicity and safety of PHH-1V in 240 healthy adolescents (≥ 12 to < 18 years) primed with BNT162b2. Immunogenicity (N = 90) was assessed by measuring neutralizing antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 variants and total binding antibodies in adolescent participants vs young adults (≥ 18 to ≤ 25 years) (N = 81) from a previous trial, who had also been boosted with PHH-1V. T-cell responses at day 14 post booster were also evaluated. Antibody durability and adverse events (AEs) were assessed through day 336. RESULTS: Neutralizing titers-against Omicron BA.1 (primary endpoint), WH1, Beta, and Delta variants-and total binding antibodies were significantly higher in adolescents than in young adults (P < .001), demonstrating noninferiority (margin < 1.5). T-cell responses against BA.1 and Beta also increased significantly (P < .001). Cross-variant antibody titers remained above baseline (day 0) through day 336. AEs were mostly mild/moderate, primarily injection-site pain and headache within 28 days. No related serious AEs were reported. CONCLUSIONS: As a heterologous booster in adolescents, PHH-1V is safe and elicits cellular and sustained humoral responses with cross-variant immune recognition, which support the use of PHH-1V in adolescent vaccination strategies. Data in younger and specific risk groups are still needed.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of PHH-1V as a heterologous booster in adolescents, building on its demonstrated effectiveness in adults.
analysis.study_design_and_population: HIPRA-HH-3 was a phase IIb, open-label, multicenter, noninferiority trial involving 240 healthy adolescents (≥ 12 to < 18 years) who had previously received BNT162b2 as a prime vaccine.
analysis.methods: Immunogenicity was assessed by measuring neutralizing antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 variants and total binding antibodies in adolescents compared to young adults (≥ 18 to ≤ 25 years) from a previous trial. T-cell responses were evaluated at day 14 post-booster, and antibody durability and adverse events were monitored through day 336.
analysis.main_results: Neutralizing titers against Omicron BA.1, WH1, Beta, and Delta variants, as well as total binding antibodies, were significantly higher in adolescents than in young adults (P < .001). Cross-variant antibody titers remained above baseline through day 336. Adverse events were mostly mild/moderate, with injection-site pain and headache being the most common within 28 days. No serious adverse events were reported.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that PHH-1V as a heterologous booster in adolescents elicits strong immune responses and is safe, supporting its inclusion in adolescent vaccination strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide evidence for the effectiveness and safety of PHH-1V in adolescents, which can inform vaccination strategies and contribute to broader public health efforts against SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on a specific age group and the absence of data on younger populations or specific risk groups, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is strong, with statistically significant results and a well-defined noninferiority margin.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of PHH-1V as a heterologous booster in adolescents. The phase IIb, open-label, multicenter trial involved 240 healthy adolescents who had previously received BNT162b2. Immunogenicity was assessed by measuring neutralizing antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 variants and total binding antibodies, comparing adolescents to young adults from a prior trial. T-cell responses were evaluated at day 14 post-booster, and antibody durability and adverse events were monitored through day 336. Results showed significantly higher neutralizing titers against Omicron BA.1, WH1, Beta, and Delta variants in adolescents compared to young adults (P < .001), with cross-variant antibody titers remaining above baseline. Adverse events were mostly mild/moderate, with no serious events reported. The authors concluded that PHH-1V is safe and elicits strong immune responses in adolescents, supporting its use in vaccination strategies. However, they noted the need for further data in younger populations and specific risk groups.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of PHH-1V as a heterologous booster in adolescents, building on its demonstrated effectiveness in adults.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: HIPRA-HH-3 was a phase IIb, open-label, multicenter, noninferiority trial involving 240 healthy adolescents (≥ 12 to < 18 years) who had previously received BNT162b2 as a prime vaccine.
elements_en.methods: Immunogenicity was assessed by measuring neutralizing antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 variants and total binding antibodies in adolescents compared to young adults (≥ 18 to ≤ 25 years) from a previous trial. T-cell responses were evaluated at day 14 post-booster, and antibody durability and adverse events were monitored through day 336.
elements_en.main_results: Neutralizing titers against Omicron BA.1, WH1, Beta, and Delta variants, as well as total binding antibodies, were significantly higher in adolescents than in young adults (P < .001). Cross-variant antibody titers remained above baseline through day 336. Adverse events were mostly mild/moderate, with injection-site pain and headache being the most common within 28 days. No serious adverse events were reported.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that PHH-1V as a heterologous booster in adolescents elicits strong immune responses and is safe, supporting its inclusion in adolescent vaccination strategies.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide evidence for the effectiveness and safety of PHH-1V in adolescents, which can inform vaccination strategies and contribute to broader public health efforts against SARS-CoV-2.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on a specific age group and the absence of data on younger populations or specific risk groups, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is strong, with statistically significant results and a well-defined noninferiority margin.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在以 PHH-1V 在成人中已证实的有效性为基础,评估 PHH-1V 作为异源加强剂在青少年中的免疫原性和安全性。

elements_zh.methods: 通过测量青少年与年轻成人(≥18至≤25岁)对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变异株的中和抗体以及总结合抗体,评估了免疫原性。T细胞反应在加强接种后第14天进行评估,抗体持久性和不良事件则在第336天持续监测。
elements_zh.main_results: 青少年对 Omicron BA.1、WH1、Beta 和 Delta 变异株的中和抗体滴度以及总结合抗体水平显著高于年轻成人(P < .001)。跨变异株的抗体滴度在第 336 天仍高于基线(第 0 天)。不良事件主要为轻度/中度,28 天内最常见的不良事件是注射部位疼痛和头痛。未报告严重不良事件。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,PHH-1V 作为青少年的异源加强疫苗可引发强效的 免疫应答 并且是安全的,支持其纳入青少年 疫苗接种 策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为 PHH-1V 在青少年中的有效性及安全性提供了证据,有助于制定 疫苗接种 策略,并为更广泛的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 公共卫生应对措施做出贡献。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其仅针对特定年龄组,且缺乏对更年轻人群或特定高风险群体的数据,这可能影响结果的普遍适用性。证据强度较高,具有统计学显著性结果和明确的非劣效性边界。

papers.title_zh: Immunogenicity and Safety of PHH-1V COVID-19 Vaccine as a Heterologous Booster in Adolescents.
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: PHH-1V, a protein-based, non-mRNA, bivalent, adjuvanted COVID-19 vaccine, has demonstrated strong immunogenicity and favorable safety as a booster in adults. This study evaluated PHH-1V as a heterologous booster in adolescents. METHODS: HIPRA-HH-3 was a phase IIb, open-label, multicenter, noninferiority trial assessing the immunogenicity and safety of PHH-1V in 240 healthy adolescents (≥ 12 to < 18 years) primed with BNT162b2. Immunogenicity (N = 90) was assessed by measuring neutralizing antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 variants and total binding antibodies in adolescent participants vs young adults (≥ 18 to ≤ 25 years) (N = 81) from a previous trial, who had also been boosted with PHH-1V. T-cell responses at day 14 post booster were also evaluated. Antibody durability and adverse events (AEs) were assessed through day 336. RESULTS: Neutralizing titers-against Omicron BA.1 (primary endpoint), WH1, Beta, and Delta variants-and total binding antibodies were significantly higher in adolescents than in young adults (P < .001), demonstrating noninferiority (margin < 1.5). T-cell responses against BA.1 and Beta also increased significantly (P < .001). Cross-variant antibody titers remained above baseline (day 0) through day 336. AEs were mostly mild/moderate, primarily injection-site pain and headache within 28 days. No related serious AEs were reported. CONCLUSIONS: As a heterologous booster in adolescents, PHH-1V is safe and elicits cellular and sustained humoral responses with cross-variant immune recognition, which support the use of PHH-1V in adolescent vaccination strategies. Data in younger and specific risk groups are still needed.

papers.title: Boosting hybrid immunity with intranasal live-attenuated or intramuscular mRNA vaccination prevents SARS-CoV-2 XBB.1.5 transmission
papers.abstract: Rapid antigenic evolution of SARS-CoV-2 and waning immunity have reduced antibody-mediated neutralization, enabling breakthrough infections and sustained transmission despite widespread immunity. This highlights the need for variant-adapted booster vaccines. However, pre-existing immunity may influence the magnitude and specificity of immune responses induced by variant-adapted booster vaccination. Using the Syrian hamster model, we previously described a safe and efficient mucosal vaccination approach using live attenuated viruses (LAV) based on a "One-to-Stop (OTS)" codon modification strategy. Whether OTS vaccines are suitable as effective booster vaccines in the presence of pre-existing mucosal immunity remained unaddressed. Here, we modeled pre-existing hybrid immunity in Syrian hamsters using intramuscular bivalent mRNA vaccination followed by SARS-CoV-2 infection and subsequently administered heterologous intranasal OTS-LAV or intramuscular mRNA XBB.1.5 booster vaccination. Both booster strategies significantly increased XBB.1.5-binding- and neutralizing antibodies systemically and at mucosal sites. In contrast, booster vaccination left SARS-CoV-2 specific T cell frequencies unchanged. While all hybrid-immune animals were protected from disease following XBB.1.5 challenge infection, virus transmission was completely blocked only after booster vaccination and was associated with the absence of infectious virus in nasal samples. Collectively, using OTS-LAV we provide a proof of concept that intranasal LAV vaccination can effectively boost pre-existing hybrid immunity and restrict viral transmission. These findings support the use of OTS-LAV as a heterologous booster strategy against SARS-CoV-2 and demonstrate that variant-adapted booster vaccination can efficiently limit transmission, a strategy highly desired for tackling emerging respiratory infections.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the effectiveness of variant-adapted booster vaccines in preventing SARS-CoV-2 XBB.1.5 transmission in the context of pre-existing hybrid immunity. Using a Syrian hamster model, researchers administered intranasal live-attenuated or intramuscular mRNA vaccines as boosters following initial bivalent mRNA vaccination and SARS-CoV-2 infection. The findings suggest that OTS-LAV vaccines can effectively boost pre-existing immunity and limit transmission, supporting their use as a heterologous booster strategy. However, the study is limited to an animal model, which may not fully reflect human immune responses.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的快速抗原变异和免疫力减弱降低了抗体介导的中和作用,导致突破性感染和持续传播,尽管广泛存在免疫力。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究使用叙利亚仓鼠模型来探讨在预先存在混合免疫的情况下,针对变异株的加强疫苗的有效性。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究通过肌肉内二价mRNA 疫苗接种接种后进行严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染,模拟了叙利亚仓鼠中的预先存在的混合免疫,并随后给予异源鼻内OTS-LAV或肌肉内mRNA XBB.1.5加强疫苗。
elements_zh.main_results: 两种加强策略均显著增加了全身和黏膜部位对XBB.1.5的结合和中和抗体水平。所有混合免疫动物在XBB.1.5挑战感染后均能防止疾病,但只有在接种加强疫苗后病毒传播才被完全阻断,并且与鼻腔样本中无传染性病毒的存在相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 加强疫苗未改变针对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的T细胞频率,突显了OTS-LAV加强疫苗对抗体反应的独特影响。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持将OTS-LAV作为针对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的异源加强策略,并证明针对变异株的加强疫苗能够有效限制传播,这对于应对新兴呼吸道感染是一种高度期望的策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于叙利亚仓鼠模型,这可能无法完全代表人类免疫应答。证据强度较高,因为它直接证明了加强疫苗在预防传播方面的有效性。

papers.abstract_zh: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的快速抗原变异和免疫力减弱降低了抗体介导的中和作用,导致突破性感染和持续传播,尽管广泛存在免疫力。这凸显了需要针对变异株的加强疫苗。然而,预先存在的免疫力可能影响针对变异株加强疫苗诱导的免疫反应的强度和特异性。我们之前使用叙利亚仓鼠模型描述了一种基于"One-to-Stop (OTS)"密码子修饰策略的减毒病毒(LAV)安全且有效的黏膜免疫增强方法。在存在预先存在的黏膜免疫力的情况下,OTS加强疫苗是否适合作为有效的增强策略仍未被解决。在此,我们通过肌肉内二价mRNA 疫苗接种接种后进行严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染,模拟了叙利亚仓鼠中的预先存在的混合免疫,并随后给予异源鼻内OTS-LAV或肌肉内mRNA XBB.1.5加强疫苗。两种加强策略均显著增加了全身和黏膜部位对XBB.1.5的结合和中和抗体水平。相比之下,加强疫苗未改变针对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的T细胞频率。尽管所有混合免疫动物在XBB.1.5挑战感染后均能防止疾病,但只有在接种加强疫苗后病毒传播才被完全阻断,并且与鼻腔样本中无传染性病毒的存在相关。总体而言,我们通过使用OTS-LAV提供了一个概念验证,表明鼻内LAV 疫苗接种可以有效增强预先存在的混合免疫并限制病毒传播。这些发现支持将OTS-LAV作为针对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的异源加强策略,并证明针对变异株的加强疫苗能够有效限制传播,这对于应对新兴呼吸道感染是一种高度期望的策略。

papers.title: Real-World Effectiveness of International Border Health Interventions in Mitigating the Spread of SARS-CoV-2 During the First Years of the COVID-19 Pandemic, 2020-2023: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: Many vaccine-related and nonpharmaceutical interventions, including travel-related measures, were established to mitigate the spread of SARS-CoV-2. Some countries began to impose measures on travelers from Wuhan, China, the location of the first identified COVID-19 cases, as early as December 31, 2019. The objective of this systematic review was to assess real-world effectiveness of travel-related measures in mitigating the international spread of SARS-CoV-2 during the declared public health emergency from 2020 to 2023. Inclusion criteria encompassed interventional and observational studies describing international travel-related mitigation measures and their effect on cases, hospitalizations, or deaths. Modeling studies were excluded. Electronic searches were performed using Embase (OVID), Global Health (OVID), CINAHL (EBSCOHost), Cochrane Library, Scopus, Medline (OVID), and World Health Organization COVID-19 Global Literature to identify studies published from January 1, 2020, through February 24, 2023. The ROBINS-I tool was used to assess risk of bias. A total of 37 observational studies met inclusion criteria for the review. Of these, 9 (24%) described quarantine-related interventions, 4 (11%) testing-only interventions, 6 (16%) border closures, 5 (14%) vaccination/immunity-based interventions, and 13 (35%) multiple interventions. Risk of bias was judged to be serious or critical for 14 (38%) of the studies. Comparison groups and outcomes were heterogeneous, but most described a positive effect on improving measured decreasing outcomes of interest. Although significant biases may be associated with these observational studies, international travel-related measures may have been effective in temporarily mitigating the spread of SARS-CoV-2 early in the pandemic. However, many measures became less effective as SARS-CoV-2 spread globally. In future pandemics, countries should consider designing evaluation strategies when measures are planned, before implementation.

papers.title_zh: Real-World Effectiveness of International Border Health Interventions in Mitigating the Spread of SARS-CoV-2 During the First Years of the COVID-19 Pandemic, 2020-2023: A Systematic Review.
papers.source_body_en: Many vaccine-related and nonpharmaceutical interventions, including travel-related measures, were established to mitigate the spread of SARS-CoV-2. Some countries began to impose measures on travelers from Wuhan, China, the location of the first identified COVID-19 cases, as early as December 31, 2019. The objective of this systematic review was to assess real-world effectiveness of travel-related measures in mitigating the international spread of SARS-CoV-2 during the declared public health emergency from 2020 to 2023. Inclusion criteria encompassed interventional and observational studies describing international travel-related mitigation measures and their effect on cases, hospitalizations, or deaths. Modeling studies were excluded. Electronic searches were performed using Embase (OVID), Global Health (OVID), CINAHL (EBSCOHost), Cochrane Library, Scopus, Medline (OVID), and World Health Organization COVID-19 Global Literature to identify studies published from January 1, 2020, through February 24, 2023. The ROBINS-I tool was used to assess risk of bias. A total of 37 observational studies met inclusion criteria for the review. Of these, 9 (24%) described quarantine-related interventions, 4 (11%) testing-only interventions, 6 (16%) border closures, 5 (14%) vaccination/immunity-based interventions, and 13 (35%) multiple interventions. Risk of bias was judged to be serious or critical for 14 (38%) of the studies. Comparison groups and outcomes were heterogeneous, but most described a positive effect on improving measured decreasing outcomes of interest. Although significant biases may be associated with these observational studies, international travel-related measures may have been effective in temporarily mitigating the spread of SARS-CoV-2 early in the pandemic. However, many measures became less effective as SARS-CoV-2 spread globally. In future pandemics, countries should consider designing evaluation strategies when measures are planned, before implementation.

papers.title: [Dynamics of behavioral factors and attitudes toward vaccination in moscow during the COVID-19 pandemic: from the acute phase to adaptation].
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The transition of the COVID-19 pandemic from the acute phase to adaptation was accompanied by changes in preventive behavior, institutional trust, emotional state and attitudes toward vaccination. OBJECTIVE: To analyze the dynamics of awareness, preventive behavior, trust, emotional state and attitudes toward vaccination among Moscow residents in 2021 compared with 2020. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The survey tool was developed by the WHO Regional Office for Europe with support from the University of Erfurt and adapted to the Moscow context. CATI was conducted using a stratified dual-frame sample. The article analyzes the 4th and 5th survey waves: February 2021 (n = 1038) and July-August 2021 (n = 998). RESULTS: By the 5th wave, adherence to most preventive measures decreased, especially social distancing, limiting contacts and using hand sanitizers. The proportion not wearing gloves increased sharply after the requirement was lifted. The mean self-assessment of emotional state decreased to 3.47 points; institutional assessments declined and vaccination attitudes became more polarized. CONCLUSIONS: Public health strategies should combine consistent scientific communication, targeted work with vaccine-hesitant groups and horizontal trust.

Objective To analyze the dynamics of awareness, preventive behavior, trust, emotional state and attitudes toward vaccination among Moscow residents in 2021 compared with 2020. Materials and methods The survey tool was developed by the WHO Regional Office for Europe with support from the University of Erfurt and adapted to the Moscow context. CATI was conducted using a stratified dual-frame sample. The article analyzes the 4th and 5th survey waves: February 2021 (n = 1038) and July-August 2021 (n = 998). Results By the 5th wave, adherence to most preventive measures decreased, especially social distancing, limiting contacts and using hand sanitizers. The proportion not wearing gloves increased sharply after the requirement was lifted. The mean self-assessment of emotional state decreased to 3.47 points; institutional assessments declined and vaccination attitudes became more polarized. Conclusions Public health strategies should combine consistent scientific communication, targeted work with vaccine-hesitant groups and horizontal trust.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of production and kinetic assay conditions and parameters for SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro): a systematic review
papers.abstract: Abstract The main protease (Mpro) of SARS-CoV-2 plays a crucial role in the viral replication cycle and is a key target for COVID-19 antiviral drugs. In this review, we conducted an extensive bibliographic search on the main challenges and experimental limitations reported in the production and biochemical characterization of the Mpro. A large variability in the kinetic parameters was revealed, which compromises comparisons across various studies and the evaluation of inhibitor efficacy. The studies indicate that these discrepancies are mainly associated with experimental limitations, such as low substrate solubility, optical irregularity due to the inner-filter effect, and variations in the oligomeric state of Mpro. This review summarizes and discusses the different strategies for Mpro expression in Escherichia coli and purification, with emphasis on obtaining an N-terminal tag-free enzyme, essential for homodimerization into a highly active form for structural and functional characterization. The main FRET-based substrates used in enzymatic assays were compiled and analyzed, as well as alternative methodologies for assessing Mpro enzymatic activity. Furthermore, the effects of assay conditions, such as buffer composition, pH, and the presence of reducing agents were addressed. The intrinsic structural features of Mpro that impact its catalytic function are discussed, including functional asymmetry in substrate binding and the positive allosteric cooperation between monomers. Overall, this review provides a critical and integrated perspective on the main experimental limitations in the production and characterization of Mpro, applicable to other proteases, contributing to the standardization of approaches and advances in the development of more effective inhibitors.

source_records.abstract: The main protease (Mpro) of SARS-CoV-2 plays a crucial role in the viral replication cycle and is a key target for COVID-19 antiviral drugs. In this review, we conducted an extensive bibliographic search on the main challenges and experimental limitations reported in the production and biochemical characterization of the Mpro. A large variability in the kinetic parameters was revealed, which compromises comparisons across various studies and the evaluation of inhibitor efficacy. The studies indicate that these discrepancies are mainly associated with experimental limitations, such as low substrate solubility, optical irregularity due to the inner-filter effect, and variations in the oligomeric state of Mpro. This review summarizes and discusses the different strategies for Mpro expression in Escherichia coli and purification, with emphasis on obtaining an N-terminal tag-free enzyme, essential for homodimerization into a highly active form for structural and functional characterization. The main FRET-based substrates used in enzymatic assays were compiled and analyzed, as well as alternative methodologies for assessing Mpro enzymatic activity. Furthermore, the effects of assay conditions, such as buffer composition, pH, and the presence of reducing agents were addressed. The intrinsic structural features of Mpro that impact its catalytic function are discussed, including functional asymmetry in substrate binding and the positive allosteric cooperation between monomers. Overall, this review provides a critical and integrated perspective on the main experimental limitations in the production and characterization of Mpro, applicable to other proteases, contributing to the standardization of approaches and advances in the development of more effective inhibitors.

elements_zh.main_results: 综述揭示了不同研究中Mpro动力学参数存在较大差异,这影响了研究之间的比较以及抑制剂功效的评估。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些差异解释为主要由实验限制引起,例如底物溶解度低、光学不规则性以及Mpro的寡聚状态变化,强调了在Mpro研究中实现方法标准化的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现有助于标准化Mpro的生产与表征方法,这对于开发针对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的更有效的抗病毒药物抑制剂至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 综述的局限性在于依赖现有文献,且证据强度中等,因为它综合了已有研究结果而非提供原始数据。

papers.title: T-Cell Response After SARS-CoV-2 Vaccination in Patients With Hematological Malignancy.
papers.abstract: Patients with hematologic malignancies (HM) often mount poor humoral responses to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination due to their immunocompromised status. Protection against severe COVID-19 is strongly related to cellular immunity, yet vaccine-induced T-cell responses remain incompletely characterized. We conducted a systematic review of 87 studies assessing vaccine-induced T-cell response rates in HM. Across HM subtypes, 75%-87% of studies reported T-cell response rates of at least 50%. Active disease was associated with reduced T-cell responses. These findings indicate that SARS-CoV-2 vaccination can elicit cellular immunity in HM patients, including those receiving immunosuppressive therapy, supporting continued vaccination strategies even when humoral responses are suboptimal.
authors: Catharina H. M. J. van Elssen

papers.title_original: T-Cell Response After SARS-CoV-2 Vaccination in Patients With Hematological Malignancy.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on T-cell responses to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in patients with hematological malignancies (HM), particularly those with immunocompromised status. The central question is whether SARS-CoV-2 vaccination can elicit effective cellular immunity in this population, despite poor humoral responses.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis of 87 studies that evaluated vaccine-induced T-cell response rates in HM patients. The studies were selected based on their assessment of T-cell responses, and the review method involved a structured analysis of these studies to determine the overall response rates.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Across HM subtypes, 75%-87% of studies reported T-cell response rates of at least 50%. This suggests that SARS-CoV-2 vaccination can induce significant cellular immunity in HM patients, even those on immunosuppressive therapy.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Active disease was associated with reduced T-cell responses, indicating variability in vaccine effectiveness based on disease status. However, the evidence does not provide detailed mechanisms or long-term data on T-cell persistence.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: These findings support the continuation of SARS-CoV-2 vaccination strategies for HM patients, even when humoral responses are suboptimal. Further research is needed to explore the impact of active disease on T-cell responses and to investigate long-term immunity.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates T-cell responses to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in patients with hematological malignancies (HM), a population known for poor humoral immunity. A systematic analysis of 87 studies found that 75%-87% reported T-cell response rates of at least 50%, suggesting that vaccination can elicit significant cellular immunity. Active disease was linked to reduced T-cell responses, highlighting variability in vaccine effectiveness. The results support ongoing vaccination efforts for HM patients despite suboptimal humoral responses, but further research is needed to understand the long-term implications and mechanisms of T-cell immunity in this group.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述聚焦于血液系统恶性肿瘤(HM)患者对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗接种的T细胞反应,特别是免疫功能低下的患者。核心问题是:尽管体液免疫反应较差,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗接种是否能够在该人群中引发有效的细胞免疫?
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述是对87项研究的系统分析,这些研究评估了疫苗在HM患者中诱导的T细胞反应率。研究的选择基于其对T细胞反应的评估,综述方法涉及对这些研究的结构化分析,以确定总体反应率。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 在不同HM亚型中,75%-87%的研究报告了至少50%的T细胞反应率。这表明,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗接种能够在HM患者中诱导显著的细胞免疫,即使这些患者正在接受免疫抑制治疗。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 活动性疾病与T细胞反应降低相关,表明疫苗的效果可能因疾病状态而异。然而,现有证据并未提供关于T细胞持续性的详细机制或长期数据。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 这些发现支持在体液免疫反应不佳的情况下继续对HM患者实施严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗接种策略。需要进一步研究以探讨活动性疾病对T细胞反应的影响,并调查长期免疫情况。

papers.title: Aromaticity at spike position 456 affects functional immunogenicity of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant receptor-binding domain
papers.abstract: The recurrent emergence of the F456L substitution in SARS-CoV-2 Omicron sublineages has been associated with immune evasion, yet its impact on vaccine-induced immune responses remains poorly understood. Using a trimeric RBD-HR subunit vaccine platform, we investigated how residue 456 influences the functional immunogenicity of the receptor-binding domain (RBD). We found that the F456L substitution markedly reduced neutralizing antibody responses against multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants, despite maintaining comparable levels of total antigen-specific IgG, indicating a selective impairment of functional immunogenicity rather than overall antigenicity. Single-cell RNA sequencing and B-cell receptor (BCR) repertoire analyses further revealed that the F456L mutation weakened germinal center responses, reduced clonal expansion, and impaired repertoire remodeling of antigen-specific B cells. Structural modeling, biolayer interferometry, and calcium flux assays demonstrated that aromatic residues at position 456 promote effective germline BCR recognition and activation. Importantly, replacing the non-aromatic leucine residue with aromatic amino acids, including tyrosine or tryptophan, restored the neutralizing antibody-eliciting capacity of the antigen. Together, these findings identify aromaticity at residue 456 as a critical determinant of RBD functional immunogenicity and demonstrate how a single amino acid substitution can reshape B-cell responses and antibody quality. This work provides important insights for rational vaccine antigen design and advances our understanding of how site-specific mutations regulate antiviral immunity.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand how the F456L substitution in the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant affects vaccine-induced immune responses, particularly focusing on functional immunogenicity of the receptor-binding domain (RBD).
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a trimeric RBD-HR subunit vaccine platform to investigate the impact of residue 456 on the functional immunogenicity of the RBD in the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant.
analysis.methods: Single-cell RNA sequencing and B-cell receptor (BCR) repertoire analyses were employed to examine how the F456L mutation affects germinal center responses, clonal expansion, and repertoire remodeling of antigen-specific B cells.
analysis.main_results: The F456L substitution significantly reduced neutralizing antibody responses against multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants, while maintaining comparable levels of total antigen-specific IgG. Structural modeling, biolayer interferometry, and calcium flux assays showed that aromatic residues at position 456 enhance effective germline BCR recognition and activation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that aromaticity at residue 456 is a critical determinant of RBD functional immunogenicity, highlighting how a single amino acid substitution can alter B-cell responses and antibody quality.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights for improving vaccine antigen design by emphasizing the importance of residue-specific modifications in enhancing neutralizing antibody responses against SARS-CoV-2 variants.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on a specific vaccine platform and does not generalize to all vaccine types. The evidence is strong as it combines structural, functional, and immunological analyses to support its conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how the F456L substitution in the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant affects the functional immunogenicity of the receptor-binding domain (RBD). Using a trimeric RBD-HR subunit vaccine platform, the researchers found that the mutation significantly reduces neutralizing antibody responses against multiple variants, despite maintaining comparable levels of total antigen-specific IgG. Single-cell RNA sequencing and B-cell receptor (BCR) repertoire analyses revealed that the F456L mutation weakens germinal center responses, reduces clonal expansion, and impairs B-cell repertoire remodeling. Structural modeling, biolayer interferometry, and calcium flux assays demonstrated that aromatic residues at position 456 promote effective germline BCR recognition and activation. Replacing the non-aromatic leucine with aromatic amino acids like tyrosine or tryptophan restored the neutralizing antibody-eliciting capacity of the antigen. These findings highlight the importance of residue-specific modifications in vaccine design and show how a single amino acid change can impact B-cell responses and antibody quality. The study's evidence is strong, but its conclusions are limited to the specific vaccine platform used.

elements_zh.main_results: F456L取代显著降低了针对多种严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变体的中和抗体反应,而总抗原特异性IgG水平保持相当。结构建模、生物层干涉技术和钙离子流实验显示,第456位芳香残基增强了有效的生源BCR识别和激活。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,第456位的芳香性是RBD功能性免疫原性的关键决定因素,突显了单个氨基酸取代如何改变B细胞反应和抗体质量。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为改进疫苗抗原设计提供了见解,强调了针对特定残基的修饰在增强针对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变体的中和抗体反应中的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其专注于特定的疫苗平台,无法推广到所有疫苗类型。其证据强度较高,因为它结合了结构、功能和免疫学分析来支持其结论。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand how the F456L substitution in the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant affects vaccine-induced immune responses, particularly focusing on functional immunogenicity of the receptor-binding domain (RBD).
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study used a trimeric RBD-HR subunit vaccine platform to investigate the impact of residue 456 on the functional immunogenicity of the RBD in the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant.
analysis_en.methods: Single-cell RNA sequencing and B-cell receptor (BCR) repertoire analyses were employed to examine how the F456L mutation affects germinal center responses, clonal expansion, and repertoire remodeling of antigen-specific B cells.
analysis_en.main_results: The F456L substitution significantly reduced neutralizing antibody responses against multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants, while maintaining comparable levels of total antigen-specific IgG. Structural modeling, biolayer interferometry, and calcium flux assays showed that aromatic residues at position 456 enhance effective germline BCR recognition and activation.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that aromaticity at residue 456 is a critical determinant of RBD functional immunogenicity, highlighting how a single amino acid substitution can alter B-cell responses and antibody quality.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights for improving vaccine antigen design by emphasizing the importance of residue-specific modifications in enhancing neutralizing antibody responses against SARS-CoV-2 variants.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on a specific vaccine platform and does not generalize to all vaccine types. The evidence is strong as it combines structural, functional, and immunological analyses to support its conclusions.

papers.title_zh: 刺突蛋白第456位芳香性影响严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2奥密克戎变体受体结合域的功能免疫原性
papers.source_body_en: The recurrent emergence of the F456L substitution in SARS-CoV-2 Omicron sublineages has been associated with immune evasion, yet its impact on vaccine-induced immune responses remains poorly understood. Using a trimeric RBD-HR subunit vaccine platform, we investigated how residue 456 influences the functional immunogenicity of the receptor-binding domain (RBD). We found that the F456L substitution markedly reduced neutralizing antibody responses against multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants, despite maintaining comparable levels of total antigen-specific IgG, indicating a selective impairment of functional immunogenicity rather than overall antigenicity. Single-cell RNA sequencing and B-cell receptor (BCR) repertoire analyses further revealed that the F456L mutation weakened germinal center responses, reduced clonal expansion, and impaired repertoire remodeling of antigen-specific B cells. Structural modeling, biolayer interferometry, and calcium flux assays demonstrated that aromatic residues at position 456 promote effective germline BCR recognition and activation. Importantly, replacing the non-aromatic leucine residue with aromatic amino acids, including tyrosine or tryptophan, restored the neutralizing antibody-eliciting capacity of the antigen. Together, these findings identify aromaticity at residue 456 as a critical determinant of RBD functional immunogenicity and demonstrate how a single amino acid substitution can reshape B-cell responses and antibody quality. This work provides important insights for rational vaccine antigen design and advances our understanding of how site-specific mutations regulate antiviral immunity.
papers.abstract_zh: F456L取代在严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2奥密克戎亚系中反复出现,与免疫逃逸有关,但其对疫苗诱导的免疫应答的影响仍不明确。我们使用三聚体RBD-HR亚单位疫苗平台,研究了第456位残基如何影响受体结合域(RBD)的功能免疫原性。我们发现,F456L取代显著降低了针对多种严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变体的中和抗体反应,尽管总抗原特异性IgG水平保持相当,这表明功能性免疫原性的选择性受损,而非整体抗原性。单细胞RNA测序和B细胞受体(BCR)谱分析进一步揭示,F456L取代削弱了生发中心反应,减少了克隆扩增,并损害了抗原特异性B细胞谱的重塑。结构建模、生物层干涉技术和钙离子流实验表明,第456位芳香残基促进了有效的生源BCR识别和激活。重要的是,将非芳香性亮氨酸残基替换为芳香族氨基酸(如酪氨酸或色氨酸)恢复了抗原的中和抗体诱导能力。综上所述,这些发现确定了第456位芳香性是RBD功能性免疫原性的关键决定因素,并展示了单个氨基酸取代如何重塑B细胞反应和抗体质量。这项工作为合理设计疫苗抗原提供了重要见解,并加深了我们对特定位点突变如何调控抗病毒药物免疫的理解。

papers.title: Differences between Canadian parents' attitudes toward routine, influenza, and COVID-19 vaccines for their children, and changes in vaccine hesitancy since the pandemic: A national cross-sectional comparative study.
papers.abstract: Background Evidence suggests the COVID-19 pandemic had heterogeneous and vaccine-specific effects on parental attitudes toward childhood vaccination. A decline in vaccine confidence has been noted in some settings, however even studies reporting stable or increased confidence suggest polarized attitudes with stronger pro- and anti-vaccine views emerging concurrently. We explored differences between Canadian parents' attitudes toward childhood routine, influenza, and COVID-19 vaccination, and changes in attitudes since the pandemic. Methods In 2025 we conducted a cross-sectional national online survey of parents with children aged 0-17 years using a polling firm. Previously validated questions asked about parents' attitudes toward vaccination using the '5C' scale, capturing separate responses for routine, influenza, and COVID-19 vaccines. We assessed changes in attitudes about routine vaccination over time by comparing 5C responses from two previous surveys conducted in 2020 and 2021. We calculated proportions and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Respondents (N = 1327) were proportionally representative across provinces, but not the territories. Parents were most confident in the safety of routine vaccines (71.0%, 95%CI 66.5-75.7), compared to influenza (63.7%, 95%CI 59.5-68.1) and COVID-19 (57.9%, 95%CI 53.9-62.1). The majority indicated the pandemic did not change attitudes about routine (60.8%) or influenza (63.7%) vaccination, while more than one-quarter (31.6% and 27.8%) reported that routine and influenza vaccines were more important following the pandemic. In 2025, a slightly higher proportion of parents reported low confidence in the safety and effectiveness of routine vaccines (12.7% and 9.2%, respectively), compared to 2021 (8.5% and 5.6%), and 2020 (12.2% and 6.8%). Conclusions Parental attitudes toward childhood COVID-19 vaccination differed from attitudes toward routine and influenza. Most parents reported positive or neutral impact of the pandemic on perceived importance of routine and influenza vaccines. Parents reported the highest positive attitudes toward routine vaccination mid-pandemic (2021), and parents' attitudes in 2025 were slightly less positive than in 2020 and 2021.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines differences in Canadian parents' attitudes toward routine, influenza, and COVID-19 vaccines for their children, and changes in vaccine hesitancy since the pandemic. The research highlights that parental confidence in routine vaccines remains higher than for influenza and COVID-19 vaccines. While the majority of parents reported no change in attitudes toward routine or influenza vaccination, some indicated increased perceived importance of these vaccines post-pandemic. The study also notes a slight increase in low confidence for routine vaccines in 2025 compared to 2021 and 2020. Overall, the findings suggest polarized attitudes toward vaccination, with stronger pro- and anti-vaccine views emerging concurrently. The study underscores the need for targeted research and public health strategies to address vaccine hesitancy and improve vaccination rates.

papers.title: Supramolecular assembly and membrane anchoring alter variant-induced SARS-CoV-2 Spike conformational dynamics.
papers.abstract: Viral surface glycoproteins function within crowded, membrane-anchored supramolecular assemblies, yet their dynamics are often inferred from soluble, engineered ectodomains. For SARS-CoV-2 Spike (S), this distinction is especially important because variant mutations evolved in the context of intact virions, not engineered trimers. Here, we combined cyclic ion mobility mass spectrometry (CIM-MS) for hydrogen deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDXMS) with computational weighted ensemble molecular dynamic (WE-MD) simulations to compare the conformational effects of SARS-CoV-2 mutations in two S protein constructs: soluble recombinant 2P S and full-length S displayed in virus-like particles (VLPs). Our results reveal that membrane anchoring and virion-like assembly substantially dampen global dynamic changes produced by variant mutations. In VLP S, D614G induced decreased dynamics across interprotomer contacts, whereas Omicron BA.1 mutations systematically reversed this decrease in dynamics in the S1 domain while preserving decreased dynamics near the fusion machinery. These effects are more spatially constrained than those observed in recombinant 2P S. Comparison of the 2 constructs further reveals that 2P substitutions alter native interprotomer communication. Recombinant S shows a predominantly fast-exchanging population in the receptor binding domain (RBD) hinge region, consistent with disruption of hydrogen-bonding and salt bridge networks that couple RBD motion to the trimer core. Thus, recombinant S captures important structural features of S without recapitulating the native conformational ensemble presented on virions. Together, these results show that the supramolecular context of S reshapes the conformational dynamics of variant evolution with direct implications for epitope presentation, antibody recognition, and interpretation of recombinant S structural studies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate how supramolecular assembly and membrane anchoring influence the conformational dynamics of SARS-CoV-2 Spike proteins, particularly in the context of viral variants, as these factors are often overlooked in soluble, engineered ectodomain studies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study compared conformational dynamics of SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein in two constructs: soluble recombinant 2P S and full-length S displayed in virus-like particles (VLPs). The research was conducted using computational and experimental methods to analyze the effects of variant mutations on these constructs.
analysis.methods: The study combined cyclic ion mobility mass spectrometry (CIM-MS) for hydrogen deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDXMS) with computational weighted ensemble molecular dynamic (WE-MD) simulations to assess conformational changes in the Spike protein caused by variant mutations.
analysis.main_results: The results showed that membrane anchoring and virion-like assembly significantly reduced global dynamic changes induced by variant mutations. Specifically, D614G mutation decreased dynamics across interprotomer contacts in VLP S, while Omicron BA.1 mutations reversed this decrease in the S1 domain but preserved reduced dynamics near the fusion machinery.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the supramolecular context of the Spike protein alters the conformational dynamics of variant evolution, which has direct implications for epitope presentation, antibody recognition, and the interpretation of recombinant Spike structural studies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide important insights into how the structural context of the Spike protein affects its dynamics, which can inform the design of more accurate diagnostic tools, vaccine development, and the understanding of immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 variants.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's results are based on computational and experimental methods, which may have limitations in fully capturing the complexity of native virion conformational dynamics. However, the evidence is strong and directly supports the conclusions drawn about the effects of supramolecular context on Spike protein dynamics.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how supramolecular assembly and membrane anchoring influence the conformational dynamics of SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein, particularly in the context of viral variants. Using a combination of experimental and computational methods, the researchers compared the effects of mutations on two Spike constructs: soluble recombinant 2P S and full-length S displayed in virus-like particles (VLPs). Their results show that the supramolecular context significantly dampens global dynamic changes induced by variants, with D614G reducing interprotomer dynamics and Omicron BA.1 mutations reversing this effect in the S1 domain while preserving reduced dynamics near the fusion machinery. The authors interpret these findings as highlighting the importance of native conformational ensembles in understanding Spike protein behavior, which has implications for epitope presentation, antibody recognition, and structural studies. The study's methods provide strong evidence, though limitations in fully replicating native virion dynamics may affect the generalizability of the results.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨超分子组装和膜锚定如何影响严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 刺突蛋白的构象动力学,特别是病毒变异体的背景,因为这些因素通常在可溶性、工程化的胞外结构域研究中被忽视。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究比较了严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 刺突蛋白在两种结构中的构象动力学:可溶性重组2P S和在病毒样颗粒(VLPs)中展示的全长S蛋白。研究使用了计算和实验方法来分析变异体突变对这些结构的影响。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究结合了循环离子迁移率质谱(CIM-MS)用于氢氘交换质谱(HDXMS)以及计算加权集合分子动力学(WE-MD)模拟,以评估变异体突变引起的刺突蛋白构象变化。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果表明,膜锚定和类似病毒颗粒的组装显著降低了变异体突变引起的全局动态变化。具体而言,在VLP S中,D614G变异体导致了跨亚基接触区域的动态减少,而Omicron BA.1 突变则在S1结构域中系统性地逆转了这种减少,同时保留了融合机制附近动态减少的现象。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,刺突蛋白的超分子环境改变了变异体进化的构象动力学,这对表位呈现、抗体识别以及重组刺突蛋白结构研究的解释具有直接影响。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为理解刺突蛋白的结构环境如何影响其动力学提供了重要见解,有助于设计更准确的诊断工具、疫苗开发以及对免疫应答到严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变异体的理解。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的结果基于计算和实验方法,可能无法完全捕捉天然病毒颗粒的构象动力学复杂性。然而,证据是强有力的,并直接支持了关于超分子环境对刺突蛋白动力学影响的结论。

papers.abstract_zh: 病毒表面糖蛋白在拥挤且膜锚定的超分子组装体中起作用,但其动力学通常是从可溶性、工程化的胞外结构域推断得出的。对于严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2刺突蛋白(S),这种区别尤为重要,因为变异体突变是在完整病毒颗粒的背景下进化而来的,而非工程化的三聚体。在这里,我们结合了循环离子迁移率质谱(CIM-MS)用于氢氘交换质谱(HDXMS)以及计算加权集合分子动力学(WE-MD)模拟,以比较变异体突变在两种S蛋白结构中的构象效应:可溶性重组2P S和在病毒样颗粒(VLPs)中展示的全长S蛋白。我们的结果表明,膜锚定和类似病毒颗粒的组装显著抑制了变异体突变引起的全局动态变化。在VLP S中,D614G变异体导致了跨亚基接触区域的动态减少,而Omicron BA.1 突变则系统性地逆转了S1结构域中的这种减少,同时保留了融合机制附近动态减少的现象。这些效应在重组2P S中更为空间受限。对这两种结构的比较进一步揭示了2P位点的替换改变了天然的亚基间通信。重组S蛋白在受体结合结构域(RBD)铰链区表现出主要的快速交换群体,这与破坏了将RBD运动与三聚体核心耦合的氢键和盐桥网络一致。因此,重组S蛋白捕捉了S蛋白的重要结构特征,但并未再现病毒颗粒上天然的构象动态集合。综上所述,这些结果表明S蛋白的超分子环境重塑了变异体进化的构象动力学,并对表位呈现、抗体识别以及重组刺突蛋白结构研究的解释具有直接影响。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨超分子组装和膜锚定如何影响严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 刺突蛋白的构象动力学,特别是病毒变异体的背景,因为这些因素通常在可溶性、工程化的胞外结构域研究中被忽视。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究比较了严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 刺突蛋白在两种结构中的构象动力学:可溶性重组2P S和在病毒样颗粒(VLPs)中展示的全长S蛋白。研究使用了计算和实验方法来分析变异体突变对这些结构的影响。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究结合了循环离子迁移率质谱(CIM-MS)用于氢氘交换质谱(HDXMS)以及计算加权集合分子动力学(WE-MD)模拟,以评估变异体突变引起的刺突蛋白构象变化。
analysis_zh.main_results: 结果表明,膜锚定和类似病毒颗粒的组装显著降低了变异体突变引起的全局动态变化。具体而言,在VLP S中,D614G变异体导致了跨亚基接触区域的动态减少,而Omicron BA.1 突变则在S1结构域中系统性地逆转了这种减少,同时保留了融合机制附近动态减少的现象。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,刺突蛋白的超分子环境改变了变异体进化的构象动力学,这对表位呈现、抗体识别以及重组刺突蛋白结构研究的解释具有直接影响。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为理解刺突蛋白的结构环境如何影响其动力学提供了重要见解,有助于设计更准确的诊断工具、疫苗开发以及对免疫应答到严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变异体的理解。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的结果基于计算和实验方法,可能无法完全捕捉天然病毒颗粒的构象动力学复杂性。然而,证据是强有力的,并直接支持了关于超分子环境对刺突蛋白动力学影响的结论。

papers.title: Differential expression of lung-homing chemokine receptors in severe COVID-19: distinct profiles between Alpha and Omicron.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19), caused by Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), is characterized by excessive pulmonary immune cell recruitment mediated by chemokine - chemokine receptor signaling. Variant-specific differences in lung-homing chemokine receptor expression remain insufficiently defined. METHODS: This retrospective case-control study analyzed Bronchoalveolar Lavage Fluid (BALF) samples from Intensive Care Unit (ICU) admitted patients with severe COVID-19 during the Alpha (hICU-α) and Omicron (hICU-Ο) waves, along with SARS-CoV-2 - negative controls. Messenger RNA expression of CXCR1, CXCR2, CXCR3, CCR2, and CCR6 was quantified by Real-Time quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-qPCR). Protein expression of selected receptors was assessed by western blotting in available samples. RESULTS: CXCR1 expression was significantly increased in hICU-α patients compared with controls (p = 0.02) but not in hICU-Ο patients. CXCR2 expression was elevated in both hICU-α and hICU-Ο groups versus controls (p = 0.008 and p = 0.006, respectively) and was higher in hICU-α than hICU-Ο patients (p = 0.009). CXCR3 expression was increased in both COVID-19 groups compared with controls (p = 0.03 and p = 0.001). CCR6 expression was highest in hICU-Ο patients compared with hICU-α and controls (p = 0.04 and p = 0.001). Increased CXCR2 and CXCR3 protein expression was confirmed in hICU-Ο patients. CONCLUSIONS: Severe COVID-19 is associated with variant-specific alterations in lung chemokine receptor expression, highlighting differential immune trafficking patterns during Alpha and Omicron waves.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates variant-specific differences in lung-homing chemokine receptor expression in severe COVID-19 patients during the Alpha and Omicron waves. Using Bronchoalveolar Lavage Fluid (BALF) samples from ICU patients, the researchers quantified mRNA and protein expression levels of CXCR1, CXCR2, CXCR3, CCR2, and CCR6 via RT-qPCR and western blotting. They found that CXCR1 was significantly increased in Alpha patients but not in Omicron patients. CXCR2 and CXCR3 were elevated in both groups compared to controls, with CXCR2 being higher in Alpha patients. CCR6 was highest in Omicron patients. These results suggest that severe COVID-19 is associated with variant-specific changes in chemokine receptor expression, indicating potential differences in immune trafficking patterns. The study's findings may contribute to understanding immune responses to different SARS-CoV-2 variants and could inform future therapeutic strategies. However, the retrospective design and potential for selection bias limit the confidence in the results, though the evidence is supported by clear statistical significance.

papers.title: Online COVID-19 Misinformation and Infodemic Governance During the Peak Pandemic Period: Scoping Review of Social Media Research From 2020 to 2022.
papers.abstract: Abstract Background During the COVID-19 pandemic, social media platforms became major channels for public health communication and public sensemaking, but they also enabled the rapid circulation of rumors, false claims, conspiracy narratives, and misleading health information. Research on online COVID-19 misinformation expanded rapidly during the peak pandemic period, yet the evidence base was fragmented across public health, computing, communication, and information science. Objective This scoping review synthesizes empirical research on online COVID-19 misinformation on social media during the peak pandemic period from February 2020 to October 2022. It examines how misinformation was conceptualized, which platforms and public health contexts were emphasized, and how computational methods shaped the evidence base for infodemic management. Its distinct contribution is an integrated comparison of conceptual definitions, thematic and platform concentration, the computational research pipeline, and the gap between detection and actionable infodemic governance. Methods We conducted a PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses)-informed scoping review of empirical studies indexed in PubMed and IEEE Xplore in November 2022 using COVID-19, social media platforms, and misinformation-related terms. Eligible reports were English-language, peer-reviewed empirical studies published between February 2020 and October 2022 that analyzed social media data using computational, quantitative, or social media analytic methods; the language restriction applied to the publication, not to the underlying dataset. The final synthesis included 100 studies selected from 1688 records. Results Within the included corpus, the literature was concentrated around vaccine-related discourse, public health and social measures-related misinformation, and text-based data from X (X Corp), formerly known as Twitter. Studies commonly used misinformation detection, classification, sentiment analysis, topic modeling, and network analysis. Fewer studies examined diffusion pathways, source tracing, cross-platform movement, intervention effectiveness, or platform governance. The evidence base remains more developed for detecting and describing misinformation than for evaluating actionable responses to it. Conclusions Peak-pandemic COVID-19 misinformation research produced important computational and empirical knowledge, but it remains detection-centered and unevenly connected to public health action. Future infodemiology research should link computational outputs to intervention design, risk communication, fact-checking workflows, platform moderation, multilingual and multimodal analysis, and the evaluation of infodemic governance strategies.

Objective This scoping review synthesizes empirical research on online COVID-19 misinformation on social media during the peak pandemic period from February 2020 to October 2022. It examines how misinformation was conceptualized, which platforms and public health contexts were emphasized, and how computational methods shaped the evidence base for infodemic management. Its distinct contribution is an integrated comparison of conceptual definitions, thematic and platform concentration, the computational research pipeline, and the gap between detection and actionable infodemic governance. Fewer studies examined diffusion pathways, source tracing, cross-platform movement, intervention effectiveness, or platform governance. The evidence base remains more developed for detecting and describing misinformation than for evaluating actionable responses to it. papers.title: Identification of broad-spectrum inhibitors for the cryptic binding site of SARS-CoV-2 NSP1 across multiple variants using molecular dynamics simulation
papers.abstract: Context Non-structural protein 1 (NSP1) is a critical viral virulence factor expressed early during SARS-CoV-2 infection that facilitates host immune evasion by supressing host gene expression through its interaction with the 40S ribosomal subunit. NSP1 occludes the mRNA entry channel, thereby inhibiting translation of host transcripts while selectively permitting viral mRNA translation. Recent advances in structural biology have revealed previously unrecognized cryptic binding pocket within NSP1, expanding the repertoire of viable drug targets. In this study, we systematically investigated an allosteric pocket of NSP1 as a novel intervention strategy to disrupt NSP1-mRNA interactions. Virtual screening of FDA-approved drugs identified sorafenib as a promising allosteric inhibitor. For the broad-spectrum efficacy evaluation, sorafenib inhibitory potential against a variety of clinically relevant NSP1 mutants was tested. Detailed molecular dynamics simulations of the wild-type and mutant systems showed that sorafenib binding leads to different conformational and dynamic changes, that result in protein stabilization. Residue-level fluctuation analyses indicated that sorafenib had relatively stable interactions within the allosteric pocket even in the presence of destabilizing mutations, suggesting resilience against mutation-driven resistance. We have identified allosteric targeting as a viable approach to blocking the functional role of NSP1 in host translation shutdown. Sorafenib emerges as a promising broad-spectrum NSP1 inhibitor for additional experimental testing and development of NSP1-directed antiviral therapeutics. Methods All FDA-approved drugs were first optimized using the semi-empirical PM6 method. The optimized structures were subsequently subjected to virtual screening against the cryptic binding site of NSP1 using AutoDock. MD simulations of the selected protein-ligand complexes were carried out using GROMACSv2023. Binding free energies were estimated using the MM/PBSA method and steered molecular dynamics simulations were performed to evaluate ligand dissociation. Post-MD trajectory analyses were performed using various built-in GROMACS tools and PyMol.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to identify broad-spectrum inhibitors targeting the cryptic binding site of SARS-CoV-2 NSP1, which is critical for host immune evasion by suppressing host gene expression through interaction with the 40S ribosomal subunit.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focused on the cryptic binding pocket of SARS-CoV-2 NSP1, examining its interactions with FDA-approved drugs and evaluating their inhibitory potential against various NSP1 mutants.
analysis.methods: FDA-approved drugs were optimized using the PM6 method, then subjected to virtual screening against the NSP1 cryptic binding site with AutoDock. Molecular dynamics simulations were conducted using GROMACSv2023, and binding free energies were estimated via the MM/PBSA method.
analysis.main_results: Sorafenib was identified as a promising allosteric inhibitor through virtual screening. Molecular dynamics simulations showed that sorafenib binding leads to conformational and dynamic changes in NSP1, resulting in protein stabilization.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that allosteric targeting of NSP1 could effectively block its functional role in host translation shutdown, offering a novel strategy for antiviral therapeutics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeting NSP1's cryptic binding site with drugs like sorafenib could provide a broad-spectrum approach to combat SARS-CoV-2 variants, potentially informing future antiviral drug development.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to computational methods and does not include experimental validation, which reduces the strength of the evidence to moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the identification of broad-spectrum inhibitors for the cryptic binding site of SARS-CoV-2 NSP1, a key virulence factor involved in host immune evasion. Using molecular dynamics simulations and virtual screening, the authors identified sorafenib as a promising candidate that stabilizes NSP1 even in the presence of mutations. The findings suggest that targeting this site could offer a novel strategy for antiviral therapeutics. However, the study relies solely on computational methods without experimental validation, limiting the strength of the evidence to moderate.

elements_zh.main_results: 通过虚拟筛选,确定索拉非尼(sorafenib)为一种有前景的变构抑制剂。分子动力学模拟显示,索拉非尼结合会导致NSP1的构象和动态变化,从而实现蛋白质稳定化。

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于计算方法,不包括实验验证,这将证据的强度降低到中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 非结构蛋白 1 (NSP1) 是 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染早期表达的关键病毒毒力因子,通过与 40S 核糖体亚基相互作用抑制 宿主 基因表达,从而促进 宿主 免疫逃避。NSP1 阻断 mRNA 进入通道,从而抑制 宿主 转录物的翻译,同时选择性地允许病毒 mRNA 翻译。结构生物学的最新进展揭示了 NSP1 内以前未被识别的神秘结合袋,扩大了可行药物靶点的范围。在这项研究中,我们系统地研究了 NSP1 的变构袋,作为破坏 NSP1-mRNA 相互作用的新干预策略。对 FDA 批准药物的虚拟筛选发现索拉非尼是一种有前途的变构抑制剂。为了进行广谱疗效评估,测试了索拉非尼对多种临床相关 NSP1 突变体的抑制潜力。对野生型和突变体系统的详细分子动力学模拟表明,索拉非尼结合导致不同的构象和动态变化,从而导致蛋白质稳定。残留水平波动分析表明,即使存在不稳定的 突变,索拉非尼在变构袋内也具有相对稳定的相互作用,这表明对 突变 驱动的耐药性具有弹性。我们已经确定变构靶向是阻断 NSP1 在 宿主 翻译关闭中的功能作用的可行方法。索拉非尼作为一种有前景的广谱 NSP1 抑制剂,可用于 NSP1 导向的 抗病毒药物 疗法的额外实验测试和开发。方法 所有 FDA 批准的药物首先使用半经验 PM6 方法进行优化。随后使用 AutoDock 对优化的结构进行针对 NSP1 神秘结合位点的虚拟筛选。使用 GROMACSv2023 对选定的蛋白质-配体复合物进行 MD 模拟。使用 MM/PBSA 方法估计结合自由能,并进行引导分子动力学模拟以评估配体解离。使用各种内置 GROMACS 工具和 PyMol 进行 MD 后轨迹分析。

papers.title: Immunization with JN.1 spike protein increases the breadth of binding and neutralizing antibodies in Syrian hamsters in an immune-history dependent manner.
papers.abstract: With much of the world exposed to previous variants of SARS-CoV-2, testing of current COVID-19 vaccines in preclinical models should occur in the context of preexisting immunity to the virus. Here, we evaluated the immunogenicity and efficacy of a JN.1 variant spike (S) protein-based nanoparticle vaccine in Syrian hamsters nine months after three immunizations with Wuhan-1 prototype, prototype + BA.5, or XBB.1.5 variant COVID-19 vaccines. Serum was collected prior to and three weeks after the JN.1 immunization to measure antibody responses to different variants of SARS-CoV-2, including JN.1 and KP.2. To assess efficacy, age-matched naive and JN.1 vaccine-boosted hamsters were challenged with the KP.2 variant of SARS-CoV-2, and viral burden in the nasal turbinates, trachea, and lungs was measured. Three doses of the nanoparticle S protein vaccine induced long-lasting virus neutralizing antibody responses, and neutralization of the JN.1 and KP.2 variants of SARS-CoV-2 was associated with one or more doses of the XBB.1.5 vaccine. Subsequent immunization with the JN.1 variant vaccine boosted JN.1 and KP.2 specific antibody responses, however, the relative increase in titer was dependent on vaccine history and inversely correlated with JN.1 neutralizing titers prior to boosting. Following challenge, JN.1-boosted hamsters, regardless of their immune history or increase in JN.1 specific antibody response, were protected against the KP.2 variant with infectious virus titers averaging at or below the limit of detection in all tissues. The reductions in viral RNA levels correlated with pre-challenge serum antibody titers against KP.2. In conclusion, boosting with a variant SARS-CoV-2 vaccine is effective in a diverse immune landscape and protects against a related virus variant.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the immunogenicity and efficacy of a JN.1 variant spike protein-based nanoparticle vaccine in Syrian hamsters with preexisting immunity from prior vaccinations. The research highlights the importance of evaluating vaccines in the context of existing immunity, as the effectiveness of the JN.1 vaccine was found to be dependent on the prior vaccine history. The study demonstrates that JN.1-boosted hamsters showed protection against the KP.2 variant, with viral titers at or below the limit of detection. The results suggest that boosting with a variant vaccine can enhance immune responses, but the magnitude of this effect varies based on prior exposure. The findings have implications for vaccine development and the understanding of immune responses in the context of evolving viral variants. However, the study is limited to preclinical models and does not provide direct human clinical data.

papers.title: Persistent COVID-19 Symptoms in General Population and Healthcare Workers: Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aims COVID‐19 can cause persistent symptoms that continue after the infection, condition known as long COVID. This study aimed to identify the prevalence of persistent signs and symptoms of COVID‐19 in individuals with confirmed SARS‐CoV‐2 infection and among healthcare workers. Methods This is a systematic review with meta‐analysis guided by PRISMA and registered in PROSPERO (CRD42023460632). Cohort studies with a minimum follow‐up of 12 weeks after COVID‐19 infection were included. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Scielo, and LILACS/BVS databases and gray literature, in November 2023. Rayyan was used for article selection, and pooled prevalence meta‐analysis for each symptom was conducted in R. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle‐Ottawa Scale. Results A total of 2,456 studies were identified, with 59 articles included in the systematic review and 58 in the meta‐analysis, comprising 196,863 participants. The symptoms with the highest pooled prevalence (95% CI) were fatigue (0.29[0.24–0.36], 95% PI: 0.05–0.78) and dyspnea (0.16[0.12–0.22], 95% PI: 0.01–0.71). Conclusion Healthcare workers showed lower prevalence rates for some persistent symptoms (fatigue, dyspnea, cough, taste changes, and gastrointestinal symptoms) than the general population. Most studies were of fair quality. Despite the findings of a high prevalence of persistent symptoms, high heterogeneity remained a key limitation.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review investigates the prevalence of persistent symptoms—collectively termed long COVID—in individuals with confirmed SARS‐CoV‐2 infection, comparing the general population with healthcare workers.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The authors conducted a systematic review and meta‐analysis following PRISMA guidelines and registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD42023460632). Cohort studies with a minimum follow‐up of 12 weeks after SARS‐CoV‐2 infection were eligible. Searches were performed in PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Scielo, and LILACS/BVS, plus gray literature, up to November 2023. Rayyan was used for article selection, and pooled prevalence estimates were calculated in R. Methodological quality was appraised with the Newcastle‐Ottawa Scale.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Across 58 studies comprising 196,863 participants, the pooled prevalence of fatigue was 0.29 (95% CI 0.24–0.36) and dyspnea 0.16 (95% CI 0.12–0.22). Healthcare workers exhibited lower prevalence rates for several persistent symptoms—including fatigue, dyspnea, cough, taste changes, and gastrointestinal symptoms—than the general population.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The analysis was limited by substantial heterogeneity among studies, and most studies were rated only as fair quality, underscoring uncertainty in the pooled estimates.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The supplied evidence does not report specific research or practice implications.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta‐analysis examined the prevalence of long COVID symptoms in the general population and healthcare workers. Using PRISMA guidelines and a PROSPERO‐registered protocol, the authors included cohort studies with at least 12 weeks of follow‐up, identified 58 studies with 196,863 participants, and assessed quality with the Newcastle‐Ottawa Scale. The pooled prevalence of fatigue and dyspnea were 29% and 16%, respectively, with healthcare workers showing lower rates for several symptoms. High heterogeneity and fair study quality limit confidence in these estimates. No explicit research or practice implications were reported in the abstract.

papers.title: Serologic Testing for Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus and SARS-CoV-2 Cross-Reactive Immune Responses, the Netherlands
papers.abstract: Cross-reactive SARS-CoV-2-specific antibodies could compromise the specificity of MERS-CoV serology, potentially leading to misclassification of infection history. SARS-CoV-2 exposure induced MERS-CoV antibodies primarily targeting the conserved S2 domain, with occasional neutralizing capacity. Combining MERS-CoV S1 binding with neutralization, however, limited the influence of SARS-CoV-2-induced cross-reactivity on MERS-CoV serology.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate whether cross-reactive SARS-CoV-2-specific antibodies could affect the specificity of MERS-CoV serology, potentially leading to misclassification of infection history.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in the Netherlands and focused on individuals exposed to SARS-CoV-2, examining their immune responses to MERS-CoV.
analysis.methods: The researchers combined MERS-CoV S1 binding assays with neutralization tests to assess the impact of SARS-CoV-2-induced cross-reactivity on MERS-CoV serology.
analysis.main_results: SARS-CoV-2 exposure induced MERS-CoV antibodies primarily targeting the conserved S2 domain, with occasional neutralizing capacity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that cross-reactivity between SARS-CoV-2 and MERS-CoV may influence serological testing, but combining S1 binding with neutralization can mitigate this issue.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results highlight the importance of using combined assays to improve the accuracy of MERS-CoV serology in populations with prior SARS-CoV-2 exposure.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-level evidence, and the generalizability of findings may be constrained by the specific population and testing methods used.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the potential for SARS-CoV-2-induced cross-reactive antibodies to affect the specificity of MERS-CoV serology in the Netherlands. It found that SARS-CoV-2 exposure led to the production of MERS-CoV antibodies primarily targeting the conserved S2 domain, with some neutralizing capacity. The researchers combined MERS-CoV S1 binding assays with neutralization tests to address this cross-reactivity. The study suggests that using combined assays can improve the accuracy of MERS-CoV serology in populations with prior SARS-CoV-2 exposure. However, the findings are based on abstract-level evidence, and the study's generalizability may be limited. The results have implications for improving serological testing methods to avoid misclassification of infection history due to cross-reactivity.

elements_zh.main_results: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 暴露诱导了 MERS-CoV 抗体,主要针对保守的 S2 结构域,偶尔具有中和能力。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果强调了使用组合检测来提高先前接触过 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的人群中 MERS-CoV 血清学 准确性的重要性。
